clue.text: Asked for money? Crazy

definitions.meaning: to touch someone for money is to ask them for a loan or gift
an old informal word for slightly mad

explanation.surface: Someone begging for cash is dismissed as unhinged.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idioms: a borrower 'touches' a friend for a fiver, and a dotty person is said to be a bit touched.

clue.text: First two of theatre seats, say, will do for cast

indicators.note: First two of means the opening pair of letters of theatre are taken

parts.note: a row is a line of seats, given as an example by say

explanation.surface: The front couple of seats in a theatre will be fine for the actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like the actors in a play, but it is the verb meaning to fling.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast a stone is to hurl or fling it.

clue.text: Running round most of valley, seizing time without ramblers?

indicators.note: seizing means the jumbled letters grab the time letter inside them
running means the letters of round and the shortened valley word are set going in a new order
most of means the last letter of the valley word is dropped

parts.note: a dene is a narrow wooded valley

explanation.surface: Runners circle a valley, keeping an eye on the clock, in the absence of walkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' makes UNRODDEN, which 'seizing' wraps round T. 'Running' looks like the activity in the scene, but it only signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground never walked on has had no hikers across it, which the question mark hints at playfully.

clue.text: Criminal's bad luck, dropping half the rings

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition (a gangster) to the wordplay

indicators.note: dropping means that pair of ring letters falls out of the jinx word

parts.note: a hoodoo is a jinx or run of bad luck
the jinx word has four ring-shaped letters O, and half of them is a pair

explanation.surface: A crook's jinx ends when he loses half his rings.
explanation.definitionFit: Hood is slang, chiefly American, for a gangster or thug, short for hoodlum.

clue.text: Tries to work with addresses around accepted unemployment black spots

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters go round the accepted letter
to work means the letters of tries and addresses are worked into a new order

parts.note: A is short for accepted, as marked on a bill of exchange

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get a job by contacting places where jobs are scarce.
explanation.definitionFit: Regions of high joblessness and poverty were officially designated for aid under this name.

clue.text: Is husband following obscure unknown figure, being out-of-date?

indicators.note: the words Is and husband come after the obscuring word and the unknown in the finished word

parts.note: to fog is to obscure or cloud
Y is an algebraic unknown
H is the abbreviation for husband in family records

explanation.surface: A husband trailing a shadowy stranger seems hopelessly behind the times.
explanation.definitionFit: A fogy is a stuffy old-fashioned person, so behaving like one means being behind the times.

clue.text: Penalty also given to the current old doctor providing tool for searchers?

parts.note: a fine is a penalty
too means also
taken as written
DC is direct current
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A fine and a dated doctor's electrical treatment are handed to people hunting for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old doctor' is two pieces, not one: O for old, then MB.
explanation.definitionFit: To go over something with this implement is a common idiom for a meticulous search.

clue.text: Target of bomb: pulverised zone, with rock sent skywards

parts.note: ground means crushed to powder

indicators.note: sent skywards means the rock word reads upwards in this down answer

parts.note: ore is rock containing metal

explanation.surface: A bomb's target is a smashed area with debris flung into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: The point directly beneath an explosion, especially a nuclear one, is called this.

clue.text: Picture that is used to bind publication

indicators.note: used to bind means the that-is letters wrap round the publication word

parts.note: ie is short for id est, that is
a mag, short for magazine, is a publication

explanation.surface: An illustration is needed to hold a magazine together.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a representation such as a photograph or drawing.

clue.text: One's death is represented here

indicators.note: is represented means the letters of one's death are presented again in a new order

explanation.surface: This is where a person's passing is marked.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'One's' is ignored; the whole clue is both the anagram and a description of a grave marker.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave marker records when the person under it died, so a death is set out on it.

clue.text: Moved to a prison — having used this in food?

definitions.text: Moved to a prison — having used this in food?

indicators.note: moved means the letters of the words to a prison are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A poisoner, caught after lacing a meal, is transferred to jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: 'Moved' rearranges TO A PRISON, and the clue also describes the fate of someone who slipped this into a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who doctored food with a rodent killer could well end up behind bars, which is the scene the clue paints.

clue.text: American in House backing a Midwest city

indicators.note: backing means that combination is read from the end to the start
in means the American abbreviation sits inside the house abbreviation

explanation.surface: An American politician in the House supports a city in the Midwest.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebraska's largest city lies on the Missouri River in the American Midwest.

clue.text: Constituent of panelling in Court Department

parts.note: to court is to woo

explanation.surface: Panelling is installed in a court building's department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a noun naming a law court, but it is the verb meaning to romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Panels for walls are traditionally made of timber such as oak.

clue.text: They imagine a lot of journalists will accept offer

indicators.note: will accept means the offer word is taken inside the trimmed journalists word
a lot of, not all, means the last letter of the journalists word is dropped

parts.note: the press is the body of journalists
a tender is a formal offer or bid

explanation.surface: Reporters will take up a proposal of their own invention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They imagine' is the definition in the sense of making a claim: those who pretend. PRES is PRESS less its last S.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretenders are claimants, people who lay claim to something, such as a throne, without full right.

clue.text: Prime altar decorated in time before the wedding

indicators.note: decorated means the letters of prime altar are dressed up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The main altar is adorned ahead of the ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes anything happening before marriage, such as an engagement period.

clue.text: Article dropped by one attacking cavalryman

indicators.note: dropped by means the article is lost from the attacker word

parts.note: a raider is someone who attacks
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An attacker loses a piece of equipment while charging on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalry soldier is mounted on a horse, so is a horseman.

clue.text: Lars and Peter working to improve state of wall

indicators.note: working means the letters of the two names are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Two builders named Lars and Peter are busy fixing up a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a wall a fresh coat of render is to renew its surface.

clue.text: Soprano favouring finale of Berlioz and nothing more, using forced notes

parts.note: to be for something is to favour it

indicators.note: finale of means the last letter of Berlioz

parts.note: taken as written
nothing more, a plain zero, is the letter O

explanation.surface: A singer who prefers the end of a Berlioz piece pushes her notes hard.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian musical direction tells performers to play a note with sudden strong emphasis.

clue.text: Nearby fellow enthralled by remarkable evening

parts.note: nigh means near

indicators.note: enthralled by means the fellow letter is held inside the remarkable word

parts.note: tall, as in a tall story, means far-fetched or remarkable

explanation.surface: A neighbour is captivated by a wonderful evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk, when night comes down, is the start of the evening.

clue.text: Positive French name is applied to writer in hot, hot Asian city

indicators.note: in means the name and writer words go between the two hot abbreviations

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
H again for hot
nom is French for name
a pen is a writer's tool

explanation.surface: A confident French author's name is attached to a sweltering Asian location.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambodia's capital sits where the Mekong and Tonle Sap rivers meet.

clue.text: What makes one blush, showing some change of heart? Behaving badly

indicators.note: the middle letters of the make-up word swap places, a change in its heart

parts.note: rouge is make-up that gives a blush to the cheeks

explanation.surface: Someone who has been misbehaving reddens and shows regret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing some change of heart' swaps the U and G in the middle of ROUGE. 'Blush' pretends to be embarrassment rather than cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, as in a rogue trader, it describes someone acting wildly outside the rules.

clue.text: Lad ran goal excitedly, slowing to score

indicators.note: excitedly means the letters of lad ran goal are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A boy dashed off in triumph after scoring a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks like a football tally, but it means a written piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian term in a piece of music tells players to broaden and slow down gradually.

clue.text: Trivial insult ignored by son

indicators.note: ignored by means the son letter is left out of the insult word

parts.note: a slight is an insult or snub

explanation.surface: A son shrugs off a petty jibe.
explanation.definitionFit: Light reading or a light matter is not serious, so unimportant.

clue.text: Excessive, with no additional energy required to make the pace

indicators.note: with no additional means the extra energy letter is removed from the excessive word

parts.note: a steep price is an excessive one
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: No extra effort is needed to keep up with the speed of a walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A single stride is a pace, and the two words are interchangeable.

clue.text: It's a shame about termination of sincere expression of holiness

indicators.note: about means the shame word goes round that final letter

parts.note: it's a pity means it's a shame

indicators.note: termination of means the last letter of sincere

explanation.surface: Someone laments the end of a heartfelt religious display.
explanation.definitionFit: Devoutness shown in worship is an outward display of religious reverence.

clue.text: That fellow curtailed passion, being subject to will?

parts.note: he is that fellow

indicators.note: curtailed means the passion word loses its last letter

parts.note: ire is anger, a passion

explanation.surface: A man cut short his anger, bowing to someone's determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will' looks like willpower, but it is the legal document that names who inherits.
explanation.definitionFit: A person named to inherit in a testament is the one a bequest is directed to.

clue.text: Drunk to touch heart after diverting attention

indicators.note: after means the trimmed heart word comes after the touching word

parts.note: tig is the children's chasing game where one touches another, so to tig is to touch

indicators.note: diverting means the attention word is turned away out of the heart word

parts.note: taken as the word heart
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A drunk reaches for someone's chest after catching their eye.
explanation.walkthrough: TIG, also called tag, is a British playground chasing game. HEART loses EAR to leave HT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is informal slang for intoxicated.

clue.text: River containing single example of vermin — that's clear

indicators.note: containing means the river word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
single means one
a rat is one kind of vermin

explanation.surface: A river with a lone rat in it is pronounced free of pests.
explanation.walkthrough: The EXE is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear someone is to declare them blameless, absolving them of a charge.

clue.text: Talks idly, ceding power, providing surprises

indicators.note: ceding means the power letter is given up from the chattering word

parts.note: prattles means chatters idly
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A chatterer who gives up authority keeps springing shocks.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle or disconcert someone is to rattle them, a verb sense matching surprises.

clue.text: Stream and meadow in Lancashire town

parts.note: burn is a Scottish and northern word for a stream
a ley is a meadow or grassland

explanation.surface: A brook and grassland are found in a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire is a county in north-west England; this town is known for its football club.
explanation.definitionFit: This mill town in the north-west is in the county of Lancashire.
